Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NexCart Retail Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NexCart Retail's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Lee, CEO; Taylor Kim, CFO; Morgan Patel, COO; Sarah Chen, CMO; Riley Novak, CTO; Jordan Reyes, CDO; and Casey Green, CSO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, CEO of NexCart Retail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 2024 performance, driven by robust revenue growth outpacing guidance, exceptional seller momentum, and early wins from our new AI-powered product launches that are already reshaping customer engagement. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV up 17% year-over-year to $2.7 billion, active customers expanding, and marketplace take rates holding firm amid competitive pressures.

Our focus remains on derisking traditional seasonality through tech-enabled evergreen growth, where we've outperformed our models by double digits this year. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our NexAI Shopper, EcoThread sustainable line, and Dash15 quick-delivery service, which we believe will significantly expand our GMV run-rate and build long-term loyalty.

We are investing heavily in supply chain resilience to counter logistics disruptions, including micro-fulfillment expansions and AI routing.

We are focused on improving gross margins through private-label mix shifts and fulfillment efficiencies, hitting 37.2% this quarter.

We are expanding our presence in high-growth APAC markets with localized seller tools and partnerships.

We are enhancing our customer experience through data-driven personalization and AR try-ons.

Finally, we are committed to sustainability via verified eco-products and carbon reductions.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. Our Q2 2024 revenue was $2.7 billion, an increase of 17% year-over-year and 13% quarter-over-quarter, smashing the high end of our guidance range of flat-to-2% growth and representing our strongest top-line beat in recent quarters. This outpaced the broader e-commerce industry's 9% CAGR, fueled by a 14% GMV rise, modest AOV stability at $72, and advertising strength. Year-over-year, we grew from $2.3 billion, while sequentially we accelerated past Q1's momentum, thanks to our Summer Surge event generating $450 million incremental.

Gross margin was 37.2%, up 150 basis points year-over-year from 35.7% and 50 basis points sequentially, our fourth straight quarter of expansion with a trailing four-quarter average of 36.8%. This reflects favorable product mix with private-label at 28% of GMV delivering 45-50% margins, fulfillment costs down 12% to $4.20 per unit via 45 automated centers, supplier negotiations locking 70% of inventory pre-inflation, and disciplined dynamic pricing offsetting 22% promo depth. Regionally, North America led at 39.1%, Europe at 35.8%, and APAC at 33.4%, with initiatives like nearshoring to Mexico and Vietnam shielding us from tariffs and disruptions.

As we dive deeper into financials, I'd like to spend time on seasonality—a perennial driver shaping our GMV, margins, and operations in this space where we compete with Amazon, Shopify, and Walmart e-commerce. Historically, Q4 is 38-42% of annual GMV from holidays, Q1 drops 20-25%, Q2 builds 22-25%, Q3 ramps 25-28%, mirroring NRF and Adobe benchmarks with U.S. online holidays at $240 billion last year up 8%. In FY 2023, Q4 surged 55% to $4.2 billion with 28% AOV lift to $85 via CartComplete AI, active customers to 45 million, mobile at 72%, margins at 42% despite shipping hikes.

In 2024, we've outperformed our model by 8-10%. Q1: $2.4 billion vs. expected $2.1 billion, only 15% sequential dip on Winter Reset Rewards retaining 65% holiday shoppers, 22% repeat lift via NexAI Predict at 92% churn accuracy, U.S. tax refunds, Europe partnerships, AR try-ons cutting returns to 22%. Q2: $2.7 billion vs. $2.3 billion projected, +17% YoY on Summer Surge $450 million over Prime Day comps, AOV at $72 via dynamic pricing on 1.2 million SKUs, micro-fulfillment to 85% next-day, Ocado AI cutting last-mile 14%, category shifts like Home & Garden +25%, Electronics +20%. North America +18%, EMEA +10%, APAC +22% on Singles' Day prep despite SEA monsoons. Macro: value shift to NexOwn at 35% units 55% margins, milder recession, omnichannel BOPIS +40%.

This validates Evergreen Growth: $250 million capex in AI inventory optimization cut stockouts 25%, CAC to $28 payback 4.2 months, LTV to $420. Q3 guide $3.0-3.2 billion +12-18% YoY, Q4 $4.5 billion 40%+ of year.

Turning to seller performance, bedrock of our flywheel empowering over a million sellers to 500 million buyers in 190 countries. Ended Q2 with 1.85 million active sellers—$1,000+ GMV or 10+ orders T12M—up 28% YoY from 1.44 million, full-year average 1.72 million +32%. SMBs 68% at 1.26 million +35%, enterprises 32% at 592,000 +15%, top 1% Power Sellers 18,500 at 42% GMV. Average revenue per seller $128,400 T12M +12% YoY, full-year $119,200 +18%, median $42,700; take rate 14.2% yielding $24.6 billion services revenue +26%.

Drivers: 450,000 net new via Seller Ignition zero-fee 62% conversion, AI fraud flagging 14%; churn 8.2% via Seller Dashboard 2.0 uptake 71% GMV +24%, Sponsored Products +41% ROAS 4.8x. Categories: Electronics +29% to 538,000, Fashion +25% to 462,000 AR 18%, Grocery +52% to 185,000. Regions: NA 42% 777,000 +22% ARPU $162,000 FBN 55%; APAC 35% 648,000 +42% ARPU $89,500 NexLive $4.2B; EMEA 16% 296,000 +26% ARPU $112,000; LATAM 129,000 +38% ARPU $76,400.

Quality focus pruned 22,000 low performers, FBN 28 centers 65% orders +37% ARPU, GraphQL API v3 stockouts -29%. CAC $142 +9% but LTV:CAC 5.2x. Guide 2024: 2.1-2.3 million sellers +25-30%, ARPU $135-142,000 +10-15%, GMV $280-300 billion.

On new launches driving 12% revenue growth 15% EBITDA: NexAI Shopper late April US/EU/APAC, LLM on 15PB data visual search, $450 million incremental 8% GMV, 35% conversion uplift >25% target, AOV $128 +22%, NPS 72/2.5M interactions 4.8/5, churn <5% LTV +18%, AWS Bedrock <500ms, US 45% pen. EcoThread May 500 SKUs recycled plastics, $180 million GMV 40% margins 52% repeat 3x velocity 8.2x turns, 4.7/5 1.2M reviews blockchain verified Gen Z 62%, LTV 2.5x CAC -27%, NA 55%. Dash15 five US metros two EU 50 micro-centers robotics, $320 million GMV 65% density $4.20/order -15% DoorDash, attachment 28% AOV +$15 NPS 68 4.6/5, US 80%. Outlook $2.5-3B run-rate Q3 full impact.

Logistics costs rose to 10.2% GMV weighing margins 180bps: ocean +140% to $5,200/40ft Red Sea reroutes +28% inbound $162M NA port congestion +35% demurrage airlift 15%, Europe +110%, APAC monsoons; inland +16% $193M fuel $4.20/gal last-mile $2.87 +19%. Mitigations: nearshoring 22% shift -15% exposure, AI routing -8% spot, automation pick +40%, Flexport -11% holding, drones EV. $750M capex air charters DCs peak 10.5% Q3 to 9.5% YE.

Operating expenses were $1.8 billion, representing 67% of revenue, with marketing at 28% of budget efficient. Blended CAC $42.50 -19% YoY -7% QoQ below $55-65 industry, ROAS 4.8x LTV:CAC 3.2:1. Paid search $38.20 6.2x, social $29.80 5.5x, affiliates $25.40 4.1x, email $18.90 9.2x, CTV $65.20 2.8x. Server-side tracking first-party CDP AI DCO 87% accuracy. NA $48 5.1x, EMEA $39 -22%, APAC $22 -35%. PeakPerks retention 45% LTV $285.

Our net income for the quarter was $250 million, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $3.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of revenue $11-12 billion, GMV $11.5-12.5 billion, EBITDA margins 14-15%.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Patel to discuss operations.

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. Operationally, we focused on supply chain diversification and fulfillment network expansion with 10 new urban hubs via Flexe partnership. Our shipping times improved by 18% to 85% next-day in the U.S. Fulfillment costs were down 14% to $4.20 per order. We are implementing Ocado AI routing and robotics across 45 centers processing 70% volume, cutting empty miles 40% and returns 8% via AR predictors.

Now I'll turn it over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Morgan. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from Shop Sustainably on TikTok/Instagram with 450 million views 3.2x lift, and Swift Week generating $4.2 billion GMV. Customer acquisition costs were $28, down 12%. Our brand awareness increased by 18% to 42% recall per Nielsen/Kantar, share of voice 14%. We are focusing on AI personalization and social commerce, adding 1.8 million new customers +22% YoY, ROAS 4.8x LTV $245 8.75:1. Paid search 6.2x conv 4.1%, social 5.1x TikTok 420k new, affiliates 7.2x. NA app +40%, Europe SEO +35%, APAC 45% +8.2x. First-party 75% consent mix modeling cut waste 22%.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Novak.

Riley Novak:
Thanks, Sarah. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI-driven personalization like NexAI Shopper LLM on 15PB data sub-500ms Bedrock, and micro-fulfillment robotics pick rates 1,200/hour. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 45%. We're investing in GraphQL API v3, edge computing Cloudflare, and Privacy Sandbox for cookieless attribution.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan Reyes.

Jordan Reyes:
Thanks, Riley. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 35% improvement in conversion rates because of NexAI Predict and propensity models at 87% accuracy on TensorFlow Snowflake. We are also focusing on first-party CDP Tealium 75% consent and GDPR-compliant zero-party for churn forecasting 92%.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Green.

Casey Green:
Thanks, Jordan. Sustainability is very important to us. We reduced our carbon footprint by 25% through DHL GoGreen and EV fleets 15%. We are committed to blockchain traceability for EcoThread recycled materials and carbon-neutral shipping qualifying for EU CBAM exemptions.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question and answer session. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from Mike Thompson with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Thompson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Taylor, can you expand on the seasonality deviations and how they inform Q3/Q4 guidance?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Mike. As detailed, we've decoupled from troughs via loyalty like Winter Reset 65% retention and Summer Surge $450 million, with regional strengths like APAC Singles' Day. Q3 $3.0-3.2 billion +12-18%, Q4 $4.5 billion on 20% traffic, risks port strikes but upside Cyber Week+.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
Great, thanks. On new launches, early NPS is impressive—any color on cross-sell and expansion plans?

Taylor Kim:
Absolutely, Lisa. NexAI 35% conv uplift AOV $128 drives 3x Dash15 attachment, EcoThread LTV 2.5x. Expanding Dash15 Singapore Mumbai Q4, voice to NexAI, full $2.5-3B run-rate.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan.

David Patel:
Thanks. Morgan, on ops—how are you mitigating ongoing supply disruptions in logistics costs?

Morgan Patel:
David, we've shifted 22% China volume to Mexico/Vietnam, AI dynamic routing -8% spot via Maersk APIs, automation +40% pick, Flexport visibility -11% holding. Peak at 10.5% Q3 to 9.5% YE.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rivera with Barclays.

Emily Rivera:
Hi, thanks. Sarah, marketing effectiveness—brand lift details and CAC sustainability?

Sarah Chen:
Emily, Shop Sustainably 450M views 3.2x lift 42% recall, ROAS 4.8x CAC $28 via AI DCO server-side. Q4 5.2x with WhatsApp AI EMs, 20-25% acquisition growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Novak with Bank of America.

Chris Novak:
Thanks. Riley, tech investments—uptime and mobile gains from what specifically?

Riley Novak:
Chris, 99.99% uptime from Cloudflare edge, mobile +45% via NexAI app integrations Mandarin/Hindi, robotics Ocado grid.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Reyes with Citi.

Alex Reyes:
Good quarter. Jordan R, data initiatives—conversion lift breakdown?

Jordan Reyes:
Alex, 35% conv from propensity 87% ML BigQuery, NexAI bundling, first-party CDP cut waste, cohort retention 45% Day-30.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Green with UBS.

Sophia Green:
Thanks. Casey, sustainability metrics—carbon reduction details and monetization?

Casey Green:
Sophia, 25% footprint cut EV 15% DHL GoGreen, EcoThread blockchain 18% premium, CBAM exemptions 2026.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jordan Lee for closing remarks.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Seasonality impact: Analyze trends and explain deviations.
New product or service launches: Early performance and customer feedback.
Seller performance metrics: Number of active sellers, revenue per seller.
Gross margin: Trends and factors influencing gross margin.
Customer acquisition cost (CAC): Efficiency and ROI of marketing spend.
Effectiveness of marketing campaigns: Brand awareness and customer acquisition.
Revenue growth (YoY and QoQ): Report actuals vs. guidance.
Logistics and shipping costs: Impact of supply chain disruptions.

aspect_summary.Seasonality impact: Outperformed seasonal models by 8-10% in 2024; Q1 GMV $2.4B vs. $2.1B expected (15% dip vs. historical 20-25%), Q2 $2.7B vs. $2.3B projected (+17% YoY); deviations from loyalty programs (Winter Reset 65% retention, Summer Surge $450M), AI optimizations, regional diversification (APAC +22%), milder recession; Q3 guide $3.0-3.2B +12-18% YoY, Q4 $4.5B.
aspect_summary.New product or service launches: NexAI Shopper (late April): $450M incremental GMV (8%), 35% conversion uplift, AOV +22% to $128, NPS 4.8/5 (72/100), LTV +18%, churn <5%; EcoThread (May, 500 SKUs): $180M GMV, 52% repeat, 4.7/5 reviews (1.2M), LTV 2.5x CAC; Dash15 (5 US/2 EU metros): $320M GMV, NPS 4.6/5 (68/100), 28% attachment, AOV +$15; combined $2.5-3B Q3 run-rate, strong early NPS and cross-sell.
aspect_summary.Seller performance metrics: 1.85M active sellers (+28% YoY from 1.44M), average revenue per seller $128,400 T12M (+12% YoY), median $42,700; SMBs 68% (+35%), enterprises 32% (+15%); drivers: 450k net new, 8.2% churn, category/region growth; FY24 guide: 2.1-2.3M (+25-30%), ARPU $135-142k (+10-15%).
aspect_summary.Gross margin: 37.2% (+150bps YoY from 35.7%, +50bps QoQ), 4th straight quarter expansion (TTM avg 36.8%); factors: private-label 28% GMV (45-50% margins), fulfillment -12% to $4.20/unit (45 centers), supplier negotiations (70% pre-inflation), dynamic pricing offsetting promos; regional: NA 39.1%, Europe 35.8%, APAC 33.4%; nearshoring shielded disruptions.
aspect_summary.Customer acquisition cost (CAC): Efficie: Blended CAC $42.50 (-19% YoY, -7% QoQ, below industry $55-65), also reported $28 (-12%); ROAS 4.8x, LTV:CAC 3.2:1 to 8.75:1; channel efficiency: paid search $38.20/6.2x, social $29.80/5.5x, email $18.90/9.2x; seller CAC $142 (+9%, LTV:CAC 5.2x); improvements via AI DCO, first-party CDP (87% accuracy), server-side tracking.
aspect_summary.Effectiveness of marketing campaigns: Br: +1.8M new customers (+22% YoY); brand awareness +18% to 42% recall (Nielsen/Kantar), share of voice 14%; campaigns: Shop Sustainably (TikTok/Instagram, 450M views, 3.2x lift), Summer Surge/Swift Week ($450M-$4.2B GMV); ROAS 4.8x across channels (social 5.1x, affiliates 7.2x); AI personalization, first-party data cut waste 22%.
aspect_summary.Revenue growth (YoY and QoQ): Report act: $2.7B (+17% YoY from $2.3B, +13% QoQ), smashed high-end guidance (flat-to-2%); GMV +14-17% to $2.7B; driven by Summer Surge ($450M incremental), AOV stability $72, advertising; outpaced industry 9% CAGR; FY guide reaffirmed $11-12B.
aspect_summary.Logistics and shipping costs: Impact of: Rose to 10.2% GMV (180bps margin drag); impacts: ocean freight +140% (Red Sea +28%, NA ports +35%), APAC monsoons, fuel +19% to $4.20/gal, last-mile +19%; mitigations: nearshoring 22% shift (-15% exposure), AI routing -8%, automation +40% pick rates, Flexport -11%; fulfillment $4.20/order -14%; $750M capex, peak 10.5% Q3 to 9.5% YE.
